text:
anya: quick share — ran a hybrid AWQ+GPTQ pass with per-layer noise-floor anneal, seeing small LMΔ on long-context (>512) prompts, wanted to sync on mitigations.
quant-bot: auto-eval summary: overall perplexity +0.1, but summarization set shows -1.1% accuracy delta. uploaded per-layer stats.
matt: can you paste the per-layer table or the top offenders? curious which layers spike.
sara: top kurtosis/outlier layers are 26, 27, 28, and 40. those have fat tails and occasional activation spikes.
liam: hypothesis: outlier channels are pushing quantization scales; two quick mitigations — surgical scaling (0.9) on those layers, or noise-floor clipping at Nσ.
anya: ran a 3-way quick probe:
- scaling-only (layers 26,27,28,40 scale=0.9): summarization Δ = -0.4%
- clipping-only (noise_floor=3σ on those layers): summarization Δ = -0.9%
- scaling+clip: summarization Δ = -0.2% and small improvement on some instruction tasks.
quant-bot: exact command used:
```
python tools/quant_bake.py \ 
  --model redwood-3b \ 
  --scheme awq+gptq \ 
  --per_layer_anneal true \ 
  --noise_floor 3 \ 
  --layers 26,27,28,40 \ 
  --scale 0.9
```
matt: good — what's the latency and throughput impact? any tail p99 regressions?
anya: throughput stable (±2%), p50 +2ms on 2048-token runs, p99 unchanged within noise.
sara: we should add these per-layer masks to deployment profiles for Dedicated and add an automatic fallback to fp16 for tail requests when summarization eval fails.
liam: +1. also add a small hysteresis so we don't flip config on transient spikes. run the 50-seed summarization eval to be safe.
anya: action items: (1) export full per-layer CSV + histograms, (2) add scaling+clip config to bakeoff profiles, (3) run 50-seed summarization eval and post results, (4) stage a canary on Dedicated (2xA10) with mask enabled. I'll open the PR tonight.
matt: thanks — @quant-bot can you pin the summary and upload artifacts? :rocket:
quant-bot: pinned the summary to this thread and uploaded artifacts to /runs/2064567890/noise_floor_scan.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
